notes: Round 10 runs several tracks at once, each in its own worktree: M1 (land animals), M2 (water mobs), M3 (night mobs) and W's w3 (the game events W's first merge left out). D0's d0b (silverfish in stone, endermites from pearls, flying navigation) is merged (c0366f3a), and release 6 is built with PROTOCOL 11 (789f6d23). Never bump minecraft_net::PROTOCOL: the release step bumps it once when messages changed; if a commit changes a ToClient/ToServer message or the codec, add a line under '## Protocol' in the track log. Insert new match arms and list entries next to related ones, not at the end of lists, to keep merges small (E3-0 names the few positional lists that are appended). Record decisions in the track log. LOAD: builds run at -j 4 per slot to keep the laptop cool; never start a second cargo command, the game, or any other long CPU-heavy process. Keep to the brief: each section names the commit its file:line anchors come from, so re-check every anchor before editing; keep off the hooks the M briefs own and follow the cross-area overlaps (both in E3-0). E2's e2b (44d96765) and D0's d0b (c0366f3a) are merged, so every 'waits for e2b', 'after d0b' and 'release 6 built' in the brief is met; d0b moved lines in server.rs, world.rs, walk_path.rs, entity_view.rs and families.rs, so anchors taken before it need a re-check. The orchestrator brings track-e3 up to minecraft-survival before each segment, so the review uses git diff r10-e3n-base..HEAD as usual. SEGMENT e3n: E3-11's structure zombies and wolf armour, then E3-12's firework colours and tooltips.

groups.prompt: Track E3 group structure-zombies: build track-e3.md section E3-11 group structure-zombies. Commits: (1) 'Minecraft zombies placed by structures are finalized like zombies', (2) 'Minecraft ocean ruin drowned carry nautilus shells like vanilla'. Key points: all changes are in generator/src/feature/entities.rs. The generator cannot call the world crate, and spawning.rs is not touched (M2 and M3 own parts of it). (1) A new fn finalize_zombie(tag, random) -> bool (jockey chicken wanted) follows vanilla Zombie.finalizeSpawn's order after finalize_mob (:158), for minecraft:drowned and minecraft:zombie_villager, on ctx.region.level_random(): CanPickUpLoot and CanBreakDoors from draws at special 0; the 5% baby with its two 5% jockey draws (a fresh structure has no free chicken; the second creates a chicken with create plus finalize_mob and wraps the zombie as its Passengers); the drowned weapon (nextFloat>0.9, then nextInt(16)<10 trident, else fishing rod) or the zombie villager's armour draw plus its 1% iron weapon by nextInt(6), as in spawning.rs; one enchantment draw per filled slot. Log as decisions: special 0 and the non-Hard chance, because Library.peaceful is never set and generation sees no difficulty; no Halloween head; no handleAttributes (it uses the zombie's own random). Note in the log that igloo entities are not finalized in vanilla, while jigsaw zombie villages are (jigsaw.rs:172). (2) A drowned's empty offhand gets a nautilus_shell at nextFloat<0.03 with drop_chances.offhand 2.0. A trident holder then draws the 0.5 jockey roll; the nautilus is left for M2's m2h, so log it. Tests are listed in the section (a seeded-rate test, a draw-order test, the zombie village template test). End with the owner's steps and the kit line.

Track E3 group wolf-armour: build track-e3.md section E3-11 group wolf-armour. Commits: (1) 'Minecraft tame wolves wear wolf armour like vanilla', (2) 'Minecraft wolf armour takes a wolf's hits, cracks and breaks, and armadillo scutes mend it', (3) 'Minecraft wolves are drawn with their armour, its dye and its cracks'. Key points: (1) Wolf (wolf.rs:132) gets body_item and body_components next to collar, as HorseState keeps them. wolf_interact's tame branch (wolves.rs:362) equips wolf_armor before the dye match: owned, tame, not a baby, not already wearing; the components are copied, the stack consumed, an item.armor.equip_wolf voice, and an equip game event through EntityWorld::game_event. EntityWorld::shear_wolf_armour plus a shears arm before MobHit::Wolf (mob_actions.rs:362), shaped like the snow golem's :303: owner only, not sneaking, the armour dropped, item.armor.unequip_wolf, a shear game event, the shears worn by 1. Save with body_equipment (server_mobs.rs:1476) and drop_chances.body 2.0; load equipment.body as horses do (:654). take_deaths' wolves loop (world.rs:4798) drops it, like equines::horse_death_equipment. (2) Add a BYPASSES_WOLF_ARMOR list of the 26.3 tag members in wolf.rs. hurt_from (wolves.rs:63) uses damage.hurt_absorbed with a closure that hands the hit to the armour: damage grows by ceil(amount) against max 64 or the stack's max_damage. Crack levels sit at 0.95, 0.69 and 0.32 of the durability left; a level change plays item.wolf_armor.crack. Breaking plays item.wolf_armor.break and clears the slot. The hurt sound is item.wolf_armor.damage while the armour absorbs. The scute mend: sitting, owned, damaged; shrink 1, item.wolf_armor.repair, damage minus (int)(max*0.125). Log the scute crumbs as left if there is no server-to-client item particle path for mobs. (3) append_wolves (wolf_render.rs:183) draws adults only, with a second pass over ADULT where every cube grows by 0.2: the wolf_body armadillo_scute layer, the armadillo_scute_overlay tinted by dyed_color only when dyed, and the wolf_armor_crackiness_{low,medium,high} texture for the level. Add the five textures to mesh.rs after :565. Friends get everything through the look tag; no protocol change. Tests are listed in the section. End with the owner's steps and the kit line.
